anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved ticket, necessary and fallback because row 1 now follows the reread ticket (A), the impossibility of the goal under the current wording (B) and the retained step-2 copy when the reread fails (E), where Before always defaulted to preserve on the grounds that the spec at the head still said otherwise. Unknown moved because D's third sentence now states outright that the linked ticket could not be read and the goal behind green could not be determined; Before put the failed read one sentence earlier and closed only with "no readable ticket or stated goal supports the switch". Message moved because each menu now shows the two quoted wordings followed by exactly three sentences with no tracker IDs, where Before spread six or so sentences over three paragraphs. Viable and veto held in both. Three spots are fragile and worth pinning in the wording: C's row 1 carries "for example by indexing on the receipt number", which edges toward arguing for a row outside the three sentences, so say row text only describes what the pick does; the parenthetical "(drops the X requirement)" on the proposed-wording line is neutral now but should be required to stay a label; and D's second sentence names no ticket, which is acceptable only because the failed read lands in the third sentence, so keep the rule that the failed read is named there. The pre-menu narration now carries the judgment and its reasoning along with the tracker ID (in A); this is outside the menu and allowed, but say explicitly that it stays above the gauntlet line so it is not read as a second argument inside the menu.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved five facts and lost none. In A and E the reread ticket, or the saved copy when the reread fails, now decides row 1, where Before preserved the contract by default "until you explicitly authorize". In B the impossibility of offline search under the hosted-index wording now drives an accept recommendation. In D the failed read is named in the third sentence rather than only in the fetch narration. The message fact now holds because each menu quotes the current and proposed wording, then gives exactly three sentences with no tracker IDs, and the row descriptions are neutral; Before's rows argued, for example "the offline-search goal remains blocked". C and F kept their preserve recommendations, and F's second sentence still names the live-check requirement. The one thin spot is C: its second sentence cites the "faster-lookup target" without saying the ticket sets that goal. To make this robust, require the second sentence to attribute the goal to the ticket whenever one was read, for example "the ticket asks only for faster lookup, which an index delivers over all seven years". Also keep the rule explicit that a failed reread falls back to the saved copy and that row descriptions carry no reasons, so later edits do not drift on E or the message fact.
